items.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I had a really good band instructor, Mr. Paul Morrison, and I was exposed through his tutoring also to composition.

ctx.x: Was there a point where you decided, in your teens perhaps, that you were going to be a musician?

Not professionally. I really hadn’t made up my mind that that was the particular direction I was going to go in after my schooling. But I definitely was quite interested. Well I was probably about eight years old when I was — well two doors down the street from where I lived was a trombone player. And he played in the old days in vaudeville theatres. He used to play for the vaudeville acts in the little pit orchestra. So well I’d already started on the violin. So my mother and father were acquainted with Mr. Paul…

So they had all these instruments on the wall, just sort of hanging there, and they said, “Look up there and pick out an instrument that you think you might like to learn.” And I didn’t know really one from another basically, so I just happened to point to the trombone.
